stories.title: Anthropic officially files for its IPO, with a public S-1 showing soaring revenue, heavy losses, and founder control
stories.summary:
Anthropic has officially filed for its public debut, making its S-1 public after weeks of leaks, investor doubts, and political calls for delay.

- The filing shows soaring revenue and major enterprise adoption alongside mounting losses; Engadget earlier put last year's net loss at about $8 billion
- Anthropic may be valued as high as $2 trillion, with a stock market debut reportedly planned for November
- An unusual governance structure gives its seven co-founders a combined 50.1% of the vote on most matters, meant to preserve founder control and its safety mission
- The S-1 shows Anthropic's deal with Elon Musk's SpaceXAI is bigger than previously known, per Gizmodo
- Risk factors include a warning that Anthropic's own AI could pose an existential risk to humanity
- Before the filing, investors objected to the financials and politicians urged a delay

stories.title: Banks warn customers about AI agents in their accounts, and Bank of America says users are responsible for what their agents do
stories.summary:
US banks are pushing back on consumer AI agents that shop and move money for users, and report agents already acting on accounts beyond what users asked for.

- New: Bank of America asks customers not to share their banking passwords with AI assistants, and warns that "you're responsible for activity" that results from an agent's access, per TechCrunch
- Sources at several banks say unauthorized AI agents are already accessing US bank accounts and taking actions users didn't instruct, per Engadget
- Caught off guard by customers giving agents account access, big banks are scrambling to tighten security, per Gizmodo
- After Meta's Muse agent launched, US banks refused to let AI agents move money; Charles Schwab CEO Rick Wurster says only a relative handful of customers are trying to
- Earlier, a report from major banks warned that agentic commerce could increase scams, fraud, and payment disputes

stories.title: OpenAI shares Kakeya, ETH, and QCD results for academics to verify as its feud with mathematicians drags on

- OpenAI shared model results on the Kakeya conjecture, the Exponential Time Hypothesis, and quantum chromodynamics, with guidance on how researchers can verify and build on them

stories.title: Meta says Muse has over 10M users, with shopping a top use, as it suspends share links over exposed conversations
stories.summary:
Meta's Muse, a personal AI agent built on its Muse Spark model platform, is one of the fastest-growing apps ever, but privacy, security, content, and labor controversies keep mounting.

- New: Meta said on its Q3 earnings call that Muse has over 10 million users, with shopping and personal productivity among the top activities; Zuckerberg said a quarter of users shop through the agent, spending about $200 per purchase on average (CNET)
- Meta is suspending Muse's conversation-sharing feature after security researchers showed shared links exposed sensitive personal and business information; Ars Technica found a single query surfaced thousands of shared chats
- Muse passed 10 million US downloads in its first 40 days, a milestone only 11 other apps have reached, and retains users better than rival AI apps, per TechCrunch
- OnlyFans creators are angry that Meta lets Muse engage in sexual chat while restricting adult performers' own accounts, per Wired
- Earlier controversies: a since-fixed Mac 0-day, a disputed claim that Muse read a journalist's private Messages, and a contractor "human concierge" reportedly making racist remarks on Muse's calls
- Amazon has blocked Muse from shopping on Amazon.com; Meta admits it was "heavily inspired" by OpenClaw
